To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The HPV status of metastatic squamous-cell carcinoma of the head and neck (HNSCC) is associated with improved survival in patients treated with chemotherapy, and (2) The HPV status can be reliably assessed in metastatic tissue samples.
(a) HPV-positive OPSCC has a better response to chemotherapy than HPV-negative OPSCC; and (b) HPV-positive OPCC has improved survival following treatment with platinum-based chemotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of the interaction between an individual and his or her environment that can be applied to the prediction of health status and to the design of health care programs.
the development and application of new technologies for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment.
the role of HPV in head and neck cancer.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the HPV status of a patient's oropharyngeal squamous cell cancer is a very powerful prognostic factor.
HPV status is associated with a significant survival benefit in patients with metastatic oropharynx squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) who are treated with platinum-based chemotherapy.
HPV-positive patients with advanced head and neck cancers can benefit from chemotherapy and radiation, and that this benefit is independent of the HPV status of the tumor.
